E020203.definition: A state of physiological or psychological stress that cannot be compensated for by normal adaptive measures.

E020204.definition: A feeling of general discomfort or uneasiness, an out-of-sorts feeling.

E020205.definition: A feeling of agitation. Tending to become frustrated or upset easily.

E0203.definition: A false sensory perception in the absence of an external stimulus.

E0204.definition: Characterized by a lack of vitality or energy.

E0205.definition: Thoughts of taking one's own life.

E0206.term: Unspecified Mental, Emotional or Behavioural Problem
E0206.definition: The report describes a non-specific Mental, Emotional or Behavioural problem. Note: Please use "Appropriate Term / Code Not Available" if the report describes a specific problem but the relevant term does not exist.

E0207.definition: A usually reversible condition characterized by the acute and sudden development of confusion, illusions, movement changes, inattentiveness, agitation and hallucinations.

E0301.definition: A reduction in the number of red blood cells, the amount of hemoglobin, and/or the volume of packed red blood cells.

E030101.definition: Anemia resulting from the premature destruction of the peripheral blood red cells.

E0302.definition: A condition in which there is a deviation from or interruption of the normal coagulation properties of the blood.

E030201.definition: A pathological process where the blood starts to coagulate throughout the whole body. This depletes the body of its platelets and coagulation factors, and there is an increased risk of hemorrhage.

E0303.definition: Disruption of the integrity of the erythrocyte membrane causing release of hemoglobin.

E0304.definition: An abnormally high circulating blood volume.

E0305.definition: An abnormally low circulating blood volume.

E0306.definition: The presence of pathogenic microorganisms in the blood stream causing a rapidly progressing systemic reaction that may lead to shock. Symptoms include fever, chills, tachycardia, and increased respiratory rate. It is a medical emergency that requires urgent medical attention.

E0307.definition: A tumor-like collection of serum in the tissues.

E0308.definition: The presence of an enlarged lymph node.

E0309.definition: The white blood cell count is below the normal range, including neutropenia.

E0310.definition: The report describes a non-specific problem with the blood or lymphatic system. Note: Please use "Appropriate Term / Code Not Available" if the report describes a specific problem but the relevant term does not exist.

E0311.definition: The white blood cell count is above the normal range.

E0312.definition: Adverse events associated with the transfusion of whole blood or one of its components, most commonly a hemolytic reaction to cross-typed blood.

E0401.definition: A disorder resulting from loss of function or tissue destruction of an organ or multiple organs, arising from humoral or cellular immune responses of the individual to his own tissue constituents.

E0402.definition: A local or general reaction of an organism following contact with a specific allergen to which it has been previously exposed and to which it has become sensitized.

E040201.definition: Progression of anaphylaxis into systemic shock, which is characterized by significant reduction in tissue perfusion which leads to hypoxia and hypotension, and can lead to death if untreated.

E040202.definition: Acute immune response that occurs from exposure to an allergen. For conditions which have progressed to systemic shock, use E040201 - Anaphylactic Shock.

E040203.definition: A regionally-limited response to an antigen, which may include inflammation, induration, erythema, pruritus or pain.

E0403.definition: A deficiency of immune response or a disorder characterized by deficient immune response.

E0404.definition: Indicates that antibodies directed against nuclear antigens have been detected. Almost invariably found in systemic lupus erythematosus and are frequently found in rheumatoid arthritis, scleroderma, Sjogren's Syndrome and mixed connective tissue disease.

E0405.definition: The report describes a non-specific problem with the immune system. Note: Please use "Appropriate Term / Code Not Available" if the report describes a specific problem but the relevant term does not exist.

E0501.definition: Bulging or ballooning in an area of an artery secondary to arterial wall weakening.

E050101.definition: An aneurysm that has burst, resulting in hemorrhage into adjacent tissues.

E0502.definition: A vascular disorder characterized by thickening and hardening of the walls of the arteries. Build-up of fatty material and calcium deposition in the arterial wall resulting in partial or complete occlusion of the arterial lumen.

E0503.definition: The blockage of a blood vessel lumen by air or solid material such as blood clot or other tissues (e.g., adipose tissue, cancer cells) that have migrated from another anatomic site.

E050301.definition: The presence of bubbles of air in the vascular system; occurrence is related to the entry of air into the venous circulation following trauma or surgery.

E050302.definition: Type of embolism when lumen of vessel or ductus is occluded by part of device.

E050303.definition: The obstruction of the pulmonary artery or one of its branches by an embolus, sometimes associated with infarction of the lung.

E050304.definition: Occlusion of the lumen of a vessel by a thrombus that has migrated from a distal site via the blood stream.

E0504.definition: The leakage of body fluid or cells from the vascular system to the surrounding tissues. This process occurs either by force or as a result of a pathologic reaction (e.g., inflammation).

E0505.definition: A localized collection of blood, usually clotted, in an organ, space, or tissue, due to a break in the wall of a blood vessel.

E0506.definition: The loss of blood from the circulation, including blood loss from a device connected to a patient.

E050601.definition: A flat discoloration of the skin or a mucous membrane, larger in area than a petechia, caused by the extravasation of blood. Discolouration under the skin caused by a bleed underneath. Typically a bruise.

E050602.definition: Extensive loss of blood due to internal or external hemorrhage.

E0507.definition: The measurement of the mean left atrial pressure, as measured by a catheter introduced into the distal pulmonary artery, is high.

E0508.definition: The measurement of the mean left atrial pressure, as measured by a catheter introduced into the distal pulmonary artery, is low.

E0509.definition: Lack of oxygen in tissues, commonly due to impaired blood supply to an area of the body, resulting in impairment of tissue oxygenation.

E0510.definition: The formation of new blood vessels.

E0511.definition: Damage to a blood vessel resulting from a full thickness disruption in the integrity of the vessel wall.

E051101.definition: Damage to the venae cavae, pulmonary artery, pulmonary veins or aorta resulting from a full thickness disruption in the integrity of the vessel wall.

E0512.definition: Inflammation of any one of the blood vessels, including the ARTERIES; VEINS; and rest of the vasculature system in the body.

E0513.definition: The creation of hematoma outside the arterial wall following bleeding due to puncture of the arterial wall. Pseudoaneurysms can also occur in the heart chambers following myocardial infarction with rupture of the wall of the ventricle.

E0514.definition: The formation of a blood clot in the lumen of a vessel or heart chamber.

E0515.definition: Spontaneous or induced tear within the wall of a blood vessel.

E0516.definition: Vasoconstriction involves narrowing of a blood vessel lumen due to smooth muscle contraction in the vessel wall and leads to decreased blood flow.

E0517.definition: Widening of a blood vessel lumen due to smooth muscle relaxation in the vessel wall and leads to increased blood flow.

E0518.definition: The report describes a non-specific problem with the vascular system. Note: Please use "Appropriate Term / Code Not Available" if the report describes a specific problem but the relevant term does not exist.

E0519.definition: Inadequate blood flow to a particular area of the body.

E0601.definition: Any variation from the normal rate or rhythm (which may include the origin of the impulse and/or its subsequent propagation) in the heart.

E060101.definition: An electrocardiographic finding showing a state of cardiac standstill with no cardiac output and no ventricular depolarization.

E060102.definition: Irregular heart rhythm, usually associated with a rapid rate, that is caused by abnormal electrical activity within the atrial.

E060103.definition: A rapid heart rate, associated with a regular rhythm, that is caused by abnormal electrical activity within the atria.

E060104.definition: An abnormally slow heart rate. Thresholds for different age, gender, and patient populations exist.

E060105.definition: A cardiac beat originating from an abnormal site. These changes lead to extra or dropped heartbeats.

E060106.definition: An interference with the normal conduction of electrical impulses that control activity of the heart muscle.

E060107.definition: An electrocardiographic finding of three or more consecutive complexes of ventricular origin. The QRS complexes are wide and have an abnormal morphology. (CDISC)

E060108.definition: A pulse that beats at irregular intervals.

E060109.definition: Abnormally high heart rate. Thresholds for different age, gender, and patient populations exist.

E060110.definition: Arrhythmia characterized by chaotic contractions of the ventricular muscle.

E0602.definition: The sudden cessation of productive cardiac activity in an individual who becomes unresponsive, without normal breathing and no signs of circulation.

E0603.definition: Increase from the normal levels of cardiac enzymes.

E0604.definition: The presence of an acquired hole in the heart.

E0605.definition: Acute compression of the heart caused by increased intrapericardial pressure due to the accumulation of blood or fluid in the pericardium from rupture of the heart or great vessels, penetrating trauma, or progressive effusion.

E0606.definition: A disease of the heart muscle.

E0607.definition: Circulatory dysfunction/insufficiency due to a decrease in the force of the cardiac contractions and / or the tone of the vascular walls. Includes diastolic and systolic dysfunction.

E0608.definition: A tear located on a leaflet of a heart valve that prevents its complete closing, which can result in valvular dysfunction.

E0609.definition: Weak or absent palpable pulse due to decreased arterial pulse pressure.

E0611.definition: Inability of the heart to pump blood adequately to fill tissue metabolic requirements or the ability to do so only at an elevated filling pressure.

E0612.definition: A disorder of cardiac function caused by insufficient blood flow to the muscle tissue of the heart. The decreased blood flow may be due to narrowing of the coronary arteries, to obstruction by a thrombus, or less commonly, to diffuse narrowing of arterioles and other small vessels within the heart. Severe interruption of the blood supply to the myocardial tissue may result in necrosis of cardiac muscle (myocardial infarction).

E061201.definition: Chest pain resulting from inadequate oxygen delivery for the needs of the myocardium.

E061202.definition: A condition which occurs when blood flow decreases or stops to a part of the heart, causing damage to the heart muscle.

E0613.definition: A below normal volume of blood pumped from the right or left ventricle of the heart per unit time.

E0614.definition: A rupture in the mitral valve tissue due to traumatic or pathologic processes.

E0616.definition: Thickening of the myocardium often due to chronic pressure overload.

E0617.definition: Inflammation of the muscle tissue of the heart.

E0618.definition: An electrocardiographic finding of a change in cardiac electrical activity.

E0619.definition: Fluid collection within the pericardial sac, usually due to inflammation.

E0621.definition: Dysfunction of one of the cardiac valves, with incomplete valve closure or damage to a valve leaflet resulting in valvular backflow.

E062101.definition: Incomplete closure or damage to a valve leaflet of the aortic valve, resulting in aortic valve backflow.

E062102.definition: Incomplete closure or damage to a valve leaflet of the mitral valve, resulting in mitral valve backflow.

E062103.definition: Incomplete closure or damage to a valve leaflet of the pulmonary valve, resulting in pulmonary valve backflow.

E062104.definition: Incomplete closure or damage to a valve leaflet of the tricuspid valve, resulting in tricuspid valve backflow.

E0622.definition: Obstruction of flow across a heart valve due to immobility of the leaflets and/or a restricted orifice.

E062201.definition: Obstruction of flow across a aortic heart valve due to immobility reduced elasticity of the leaflets and/or a restricted orifice.

E062202.definition: Obstruction of flow across a mitral heart valve due to immobility reduced elasticity of the leaflets and/or a restricted orifice.

E062203.definition: Obstruction of flow across a pulmonary heart valve due to immobility reduced elasticity of the leaflets and/or a restricted orifice.

E062204.definition: Obstruction of flow across a tricuspid heart valve due to immobility reduced elasticity of the leaflets and/or a restricted orifice.

E0623.definition: The report describes a non-specific problem with the heart. Note: Please use "Appropriate Term / Code Not Available" if the report describes a specific problem but the relevant term does not exist.

E0701.definition: Progressive and life-threatening pulmonary distress in the absence of an underlying pulmonary condition, usually following major trauma or surgery. Cases of neonatal respiratory distress syndrome are not included in this definition.

E0702.definition: Blockage of air flow in the respiratory tract.

E0704.definition: The entry of foreign material past the trachea, and into the lower respiratory tract.

E0705.definition: Inflammation of the lungs due to the inhalation of solid or liquid material.

E0706.definition: A chronic respiratory disease manifested as difficulty breathing due to the narrowing of bronchial passageways.

E0707.definition: Bleeding from the bronchial wall and/or lung parenchyma.

E0708.definition: An acute or chronic inflammatory process affecting the bronchi.

E0709.definition: Sudden contraction of the smooth muscles of the bronchial wall.

E0710.definition: Interference with respiration by obstruction of the larynx or trachea.

E0711.definition: A chronic and progressive lung disorder characterized by the loss of elasticity of the bronchial tree and the air sacs, destruction of the air sacs wall, thickening of the bronchial wall, and mucous accumulation in the bronchial tree. The pathologic changes result in the disruption of the air flow in the bronchial airways. Signs and symptoms include shortness of breath, wheezing, productive cough, and chest tightness. The two main types of chronic obstructive pulmonary disease are chronic obstructive bronchitis and emphysema.

E071101.definition: A condition characterized by increase beyond normal in the size of air spaces distal to the terminal bronchioles, either from dilatation of the alveoli or from destruction of their walls.

E0712.definition: A sudden, often repetitive, spasmodic contraction of the thoracic cavity, resulting in violent release of air from the lungs, and usually accompanied by a distinctive sound.

E0713.definition: Decrease in the maximum flow rate generated during a forceful exhalation, starting from full lung inflation.

E0715.definition: Abnormal decrease of rate of breathing.

E0716.definition: Abnormal increase of rate of breathing.

E0717.definition: An uncomfortable sensation of difficulty breathing. It may present as an acute or chronic sign of an underlying respiratory or heart disorder.

E0719.definition: A decrease in the fraction of the forced vital capacity that is exhaled in a specific number of seconds.

E0721.definition: Coughing up blood from the respiratory tract.

E0722.definition: A collection of blood in the pleural cavity.

E0723.definition: An involuntary contraction of the diaphragm against closed vocal cords, producing the hic sound.

E0724.definition: Abnormally prolonged, rapid, and deep breathing.

E0725.definition: A state in which there is a reduced amount of air entering the pulmonary alveoli.

E0726.definition: A deficiency in the amount of oxygen reaching the tissues.

E0727.definition: Displacement of structures in the thoracic cavity in one direction due to increased pleural pressure on the contralateral side.

E0729.definition: Abnormal permanent enlargement of the lung air spaces distal to terminal bronchiole not resulted from wall destruction, e.g. due to loss of opposite lung.

E0730.definition: Inflammation of the throat most often caused by viral and bacterial infections.

E0731.definition: Increased amounts of fluid within the pleural cavity. Symptoms include shortness of breath, cough, and chest pain.

E0732.definition: An accumulation of pus in the pleural space

E0733.definition: An acute and/or chronic inflammation focally or diffusely affecting the lung parenchyma.

E073301.definition: Acute inflammation of the walls of the terminal bronchioles.

E0734.definition: Abnormal presence of air in the pleural cavity.

E0735.definition: Impaired or abnormal functioning of the pulmonary system causing multiple pulmonary issues.

E0736.definition: Accumulation of fluid in the lung tissues causing disturbance of the gas exchange that may lead to respiratory failure.

E0737.definition: Increased pressure within the pulmonary circulation due to lung or heart disorder.

E0738.definition: Localized necrosis of lung tissue caused by obstruction of the arterial blood supply, most often due to pulmonary embolism.

E0739.definition: A condition in which the blood pH is less than normal, secondary to impaired gas exchange.

E0740.definition: A condition in which the blood pH is greater than normal, secondary to impaired gas exchange.

E0742.definition: The significant impairment of gas exchange within the lungs resulting in hypoxia, hypercarbia, or both, to the extent that organ tissue perfusion is severely compromised.

E0743.definition: Impairment of gas exchange within the lungs secondary to a disease process, neoplasm, or trauma, possibly resulting in hypoxia, hypercarbia, or both.

E0744.definition: An infectious disease affecting the respiratory tract.

E0745.definition: A rupture in the sinus tissue due to traumatic or pathologic processes.

E0746.definition: A symptom consisting of the involuntary expulsion of air from the nose.

E0747.definition: Any kind of inflammatory process of the tonsils, pharynx, or/and larynx characterized by pain in swallowing.

E0748.definition: Condition where there are a greater number of inhalations relative to the number of exhalations.

E0749.definition: Interference with respiration by compression of the larynx, laryngopharynx or trachea, as well as of the carotid arteria or jugular veins.

E0750.definition: A condition that requires mechanical life support due to inability to breath effectively to maintain normal levels of oxygen and carbon dioxide in the body.

E0751.definition: A symptom and finding during physical examination, characterized by high-pitched, whistling sound during breathing. It results from narrowing or obstruction of the respiratory airways.  Also known as stridor.

E0752.definition: The report describes a non-specific problem with the respiratory system. Note: Please use "Appropriate Term / Code Not Available" if the report describes a specific problem but the relevant term does not exist.

E0753.definition: Mechanical or chemical injuries to the upper airways, including trachea, pharynx and larynx.

E0801.definition: A tear in the capsular bag housing the lens.

E0802.definition: Partial or complete opacity of the crystalline lens of one or both eyes that decreases visual acuity and eventually results in blindness. Some cataracts appear in infancy or in childhood, but most develop in older individuals. (Sternberg Diagnostic Surgical Pathology, 3rd ed.)

E0803.definition: Edema of the mucous membrane of the eyeball and eyelid lining.

E0804.definition: Inflammation of the conjunctiva of the eye.

E0805.definition: Clouding of the middle area of the cornea, usually as a result of scarring due to infection, injury, or inflammation.

E0806.definition: Inability to maintain corneal integrity; or corneal edema resulting from failure of the corneal endothelium to maintain detumescence.

E080701.definition: Fluid from the aqueous humor enters the corneal stroma and causes swelling.

E080702.definition: Corneal edema of inflammatory origin associated with contact lens wear and morphologically characterized by presence of epithelial microcysts.

E0808.definition: Very small, round vesicles containing fluid and cellular debris observed on the surface of the cornea under slit lamp examination in some types of corneal dystrophy and in wearers of extended wear lenses.

E0809.definition: Discrete, small lesions present in the cornea as a result of corneal inflammation and, in some cases, after soft contact lens wear especially extended-wear lenses.

E0810.definition: Superficial vascularization of the cornea with infiltration of granulation tissue.

E0811.definition: A rupture in the corneal tissue due to traumatic or pathologic processes.

E0812.definition: Replacement of corneal tissue with scar tissue as a result of injury to the deeper layers of the cornea.

E0813.definition: Complications of intraocular lens surgery; usually refers to intraocular lens contact with cornea, can be intermittent or chronic.

E0814.definition: Area of epithelial tissue loss from corneal surface; associated with inflammatory cells in the cornea and anterior chamber.

E0815.definition: A syndrome characterized by dryness of the cornea and conjunctiva. It is usually caused by a deficiency in tear production. Symptoms include a feeling of burning eyes and a possible foreign body presence in the eye.

E0816.definition: Inflammation of the intraocular fluids or tissues usually with microbial organisms.

E0818.definition: An infection of any part of the eye, including the eyelid.

E081901.definition: Injury to the epithelium of the cornea.

E081902.definition: Burn injury, including chemical burn, to any part of the eye.

E081903.definition: Separation of the inner retina layers from the underlying pigment epithelium.

E081904.definition: Damage to the retina due to toxicity, exposure to bright lights, or trauma.

E081905.definition: A usually small tearing of the retina occurring when the vitreous separates from the retina. It may lead to retinal detachment.

E081906.definition: Detachment of the vitreous humor from the retina.

E0821.definition: Feeling of grittiness or having something in the eye; frequently caused by a foreign body.

E0822.definition: Increased pressure in the eyeball due to obstruction of the outflow of aqueous humor.

E0823.definition: Hazy ring around bright lights seen by some patients with refractive error or optical defects, e.g. cataracts, or corneal swelling.

E0824.definition: Hemorrhage within the anterior chamber of the eye.

E0825.definition: An accumulation of pus in the anterior chamber of the eye.

E0826.definition: Decrease of pressure of the intraocular fluid in the eye.

E0827.definition: Increase of pressure of the intraocular fluid in the eye, also known as ocular hypertension.

E082901.definition: Keratitis due to infection, including infection by acanthamoeba.

E0830.definition: Accumulation of intraretinal fluid and protein in the macula, which may result in swelling and decreased central vision.

E0831.definition: Ocular pain which may be very intense, accompanied by corneal epithelium damage, conjunctival injection, lacrimation, blepharospasm, photophobia and hazy vision following corneal edema caused by overwear of contact lenses, principally the PMMA type.

E0833.definition: Lay term applied to any condition with dilation of conjunctival or ciliary blood vessels; innumerable causes.

E0835.definition: An acute postoperative inflammatory reaction in which a noninfectious substance enters the anterior segment and induces toxic damage to the intraocular tissues.

E0836.definition: Clinical triad of uveitis, glaucoma, and hyphema (UGH), especially associated with the insertion of an anterior chamber intraocular lens (IOL).

E0838.definition: An interference to normal eyesight without necessarily affecting visual acuity.

E083801.definition: The perception of sudden or brief bursts of light.

E083802.definition: An objective visual sensation that appears with the eyes closed and in the absence of visual light.

E083803.definition: Spots or stringy shapes in vision, often caused by deposits, aggregates, or cell fragments in the vitreous humor or lens.

E083804.definition: Increased sensitivity of the eyes to light causing discomfort or pain.

E0839.definition: Decreased ability to see to a degree that requires corrective measures

E083901.definition: The loss of visual acuity (sharpness of vision).

E083902.definition: Severely reduced visual acuity that cannot be corrected, or total loss of vision.

E083903.definition: Perception of multiple images from one object.

E0840.definition: Blood extravasation in the vitreous humor.

E0841.definition: loss or prolapse of vitreous gel.

E0842.definition: Inflammatory intraocular reaction with clouding and cells in vitreous; often accompanies inflammation of ciliary body, iris, choroid, or retina.

E0843.definition: Rupture of the fibrous strands connecting the ciliary body with the crystalline lens of the eye (usually at the time of cataract surgery).

E0844.definition: The report describes a non-specific problem with the eye(s) or vision. Note: Please use "Appropriate Term / Code Not Available" if the report describes a specific problem but the relevant term does not exist.

E0845.definition: A generic term used to describe abnormal sensations that bother the eyes like dryness, itchiness, burning, grittiness and excessive blinking.

E0848.definition: Decrease in corneal endothelial cell density.

E0849.definition: Remnant lens epithelial cell proliferation and migration to the posterior capsule.

E0901.definition: Neurophysiological and psychological symptoms caused by sudden and unexpected loud noise.

E0902.definition: Injury to the hearing mechanisms within the inner ear, caused by excessively loud noise.

E0903.definition: Partial or complete loss of the ability to detect or understand sounds resulting from damage to the outer, middle, or inner ear structures.

E090301.definition: A condition in which a person partially loses the ability to hear sounds in one or both ears.

E090302.definition: A condition in which a person completely loses the hearing in one or both ears.

E0904.definition: A noise in the ears, such as ringing, buzzing, roaring or clicking in the absence of auditory stimulation.

E0905.definition: A feeling of movement, a sensation as if the external world were revolving around the person or as if they were revolving in space (subjective vertigo). Vertigo is medically distinct from dizziness, lightheadedness, and unsteadiness.

E0906.definition: The report describes a non-specific problem with the ear or labyrinth. Note: Please use "Appropriate Term / Code Not Available" if the report describes a specific problem but the relevant term does not exist.

E090801.definition: An infectious process involving the outer ear and ear canal.

E090802.definition: An infectious process involving the middle ear, includes acute otitis media, chronic otitis media, chronic suppurative otitis media, otitis media with effusion (OME), etc.

E0909.definition: Inflammation (swelling and redness) to the middle ear.

E1001.definition: The condition of the abdomen being enlarged or swollen from internal pressure.

E1002.definition: Painful sensation in the abdominal region.

E1003.definition: Failure of the smooth muscle fibers of the gastrointestinal tract to relax at any one point of junction of one part with another.

E1004.definition: Accumulation of fluid in the peritoneal cavity. The fluid may be serous, hemorrhagic, or the result of tumor metastasis to the peritoneum.

E1005.definition: A thermal injury to the bowels.

E1006.definition: A rupture in the wall of the small or large intestine due to traumatic or pathologic processes.

E1007.definition: Irregular and infrequent or difficult evacuation of the bowels.

E1009.definition: A symptom referring to difficult and or painful swallowing.

E1010.definition: To belch, the casting of upwind from the stomach.

E1011.definition: Gas or air in the gastrointestinal tract.

E1013.definition: Thermal, chemical or radiation injury to stomach or esophagus.

E1014.definition: Bleeding originating from any part of the gastrointestinal tract.

E1015.definition: Flow in the opposite direction from normal, as the casting up of undigested food or gas from the stomach, or the backward flowing of blood into the heart, or between the chambers of the heart when a valve is incompetent.

E1018.definition: A torn, ragged, mangled wound, or an accidental cut of esophagus.

E1019.definition: Abnormally dark tarry feces containing blood, usually from gastrointestinal bleeding.

E1020.definition: Upper abdominal discomfort associated with an urge to vomit.

E1022.definition: The presence of a hole or other type of opening in the esophageal wall through which the contents of the esophagus can pass into the mediastinum.

E1023.definition: A cut or tear of the peritoneum.

E1024.definition: Inflammation of the peritoneum due to infection by bacteria or fungi.

E1025.definition: Abdominal discomfort with retrosternal pain usually associated with gastroesophageal reflux, pyrosis or dyspepsia.

E1026.definition: Leakage due to breakdown of a rectal anastomosis.

E1027.definition: Bleeding originating in the retroperitoneal area.

E1028.definition: A non-neoplastic or neoplastic (benign or malignant) disorder involving a salivary gland.

E102801.definition: The condition of not having enough saliva to keep the mouth moist.

E1029.definition: Narrowing or tightening of the esophagus

E1030.definition: The formation of sores or a break in the wall of the stomach.

E1032.definition: Forceful ejection of the contents of the stomach through the mouth.

E1033.definition: The report describes a non-specific problem with the gastrointestinal system. Note: Please use "Appropriate Term / Code Not Available" if the report describes a specific problem but the relevant term does not exist.

E1034.definition: A continual or recurrent inclination to evacuate the bowels.

E1035.definition: Free air within the peritoneal cavity.

E1101.definition: Cirrhosis of the liver caused either by destruction of the intrahepatic bile ducts (primary biliary cholangitis) or blockage of the extrahepatic bile ducts (secondary biliary cholangitis).

E1102.definition: Inflammation of the liver; usually from a viral infection, but sometimes from toxic agents.

E1103.definition: Abnormally high level of bilirubin in the blood. Excess bilirubin is associated with jaundice.

E1104.definition: Non traumatic damage to the liver parenchyma resulting in hepatic insufficiency.

E1105.definition: Sustained, and severe damage to the liver with significant loss of function.

E1106.definition: A cut or tear in the liver.

E1107.definition: The report describes a non-specific problem with the liver or biliary system. Note: Please use "Appropriate Term / Code Not Available" if the report describes a specific problem but the relevant term does not exist.

E1108.definition: Sudden unexpected leakage of bile from the liver or soft tissue.

E1201.definition: A condition resulting from the excessive loss of fluid from the body.

E1202.definition: Higher or lower than normal values for the serum electrolytes; usually affecting Na, K, Cl, Ca, CO2, BUN.

E120201.definition: Higher than normal levels of sodium in the circulating blood.

E120202.definition: Lower than normal levels of sodium in the circulating blood.

E120203.definition: Higher than normal levels of calcium in the circulating blood.

E120204.definition: Lower than normal levels of calcium in the circulating blood.

E120205.definition: Higher than normal levels of potassium in the circulating blood.

E120206.definition: Lower than normal levels of potassium in the circulating blood.

E1203.definition: Interruption or disruption of the intake of food/nutrition.

E1204.definition: A temporary and/or sudden feeling of intense body warmth, flushing, sometimes accompanied by sweating.

E1205.definition: Abnormally high level of glucose in the blood.

E120501.definition: Elevated ketones, including metabolic acidosis produced by accumulation of ketone bodies resulting from uncontrolled diabetes mellitus.

E1206.definition: Abnormally low level of glucose in the blood.

E1207.definition: Extreme thirst accompanied by chronic excessive intake of water.

E1208.definition: Repetitive loss and regain of body weight.

E1209.definition: An imbalance of one or more hormones in the body

E1210.definition: Menopause occurring spontaneously before 40 years of age

E1211.definition: Low levels of one or more vitamins in the body.

E1303.definition: Abnormal build up of fluid in the abdomen.

E1304.definition: A sudden compelling urge to urinate.

E1305.definition: An acute or chronic condition where the kidneys are not functioning normally.

E130501.definition: An acute or chronic condition that is characterized by the inability of the kidneys to adequately filter the blood resulting in uremia and electrolyte imbalances.

E1306.definition: Abnormally high concentration of non-protein nitrogen in the blood.

E1307.definition: Narrowing of any part of the urethra. With or without affecting the flow of urine.

E1308.definition: Urination at short intervals or at higher volumes; it may result from increased urine formation, decreased bladder capacity, or lower urinary tract irritation.

E1309.definition: Accumulation of urine within the bladder because of the inability to urinate.

E1310.definition: An inflammatory process affecting any part of the urinary tract, most commonly the bladder or the urethra.

E131001.definition: An inflammatory process affecting the kidney.

E1311.definition: The report describes a non-specific problem with the kidneys or urinary system. Note: Please use "Appropriate Term / Code Not Available" if the report describes a specific problem but the relevant term does not exist.

E1401.definition: Secretions from the vagina with a smell, colour, or texture which is different from normal.

E1402.definition: Having pain, tenderness or discomfort in the breast.

E1403.definition: Abnormality in the breast parenchyma, identified either by palpation or imaging. These abnormalities include calcifications, breast tissue distortion, presence of areas of density, and presence of benign or malignant tumors.

E1404.definition: Changes such as abnormal, pathological, benign, malignant, etc.

E1406.definition: A rupture in the fallopian tube due to traumatic or pathologic processes.

E140701.definition: Uterine bleeding that occurs during a time not associated with the normal menstrual period.

E140702.definition: Heavy or large blood loss during menses.

E1408.definition: Deviations from the normal process; e.g. delayed, difficult, profuse, scanty, unusual bleeding, etc.

E1409.definition: Excessive sensitivity or changes in sensitivity in the nipple(s)

E1410.definition: Ulcer that develops in the nipple.

E1411.definition: Any pelvic infection involving the upper female genital tract beyond the cervix.

E1412.definition: Abnormal connection between rectum and vagina.

E1413.definition: Difficulty, lack of desire, or pain associated with coitus.

E141301.definition: Persistent or recurrent inability to achieve or to maintain an erection during sexual activity.

E1414.definition: A rare acute life-threatening systemic bacterial noncontagious illness caused by staphylococcal exotoxins.

E1415.definition: A rupture in the uterus due to traumatic or pathologic processes.

E1416.definition: Abnormal connection between vagina and bladder.

E1417.term: Unspecified Reproductive System or Breast Problem
E1417.definition: The report describes a non-specific problem with the breasts or reproductive system. Note: Please use "Appropriate Term / Code Not Available" if the report describes a specific problem but the relevant term does not exist.

E1418.definition: Issues related to the ability to breastfeed.

E1501.definition: The unintentional or intentional loss of a pregnancy before 22 weeks gestation.

E150102.definition: The uterus is not entirely emptied of products of conception following medical or surgical pregnancy termination.

E150104.definition: Retention in uterus of an abortus.

E150105.definition: Spontaneous expulsion of a human fetus before it is viable.

E1503.definition: A subperiosteal hemorrhage limited to the surface of one cranial bone, a usually benign condition seen in the newborn as a result of bone trauma.

E1504.definition: An infection involving chorion, amnion and amniotic fluid; generally, there is also involve placental villi and from decidua.

E1505.definition: Any abnormality either hereditary or due an influence that happen during the pregnancy until the moment of birth.

E1506.definition: Pregnancy condition that happens when there is a developing fetus or embryo outside the uterus.

E1507.definition: Signs or symptoms which may be indicative of distress to a fetus, which may include repetitive variable decelerations, fetal tachycardia or bradycardia, late decelerations, or low biophysical profile.

E1508.definition: Caused by conditions such as inadequate placental function (often abruptio placentae), preeclamptic toxicity, prolapse of the umbilical cord, or complications from anesthetic administration.

E1511.definition: Anatomic abnormality manifested during the neonatal period of physical or mechanical origin.

E1514.definition: The woman became pregnant despite using a contraceptive device.

E1515.definition: Delivery of a viable infant before the normal end of gestation.

E1516.definition: A condition of the newborn marked by dyspnea with cyanosis.

E1517.definition: Appearance of anomalies and/or developmental defects due to exposure to an agent that can disturb the development of an embryo or fetus.

E1518.definition: Children affected by toxins may be due to silicone breast implants and their effects on unborn children and from breastfeeding.

E1520.definition: Inability to conceive for at least one year after trying and having unprotected sex. Causes of female infertility include endometriosis, fallopian tubes obstruction, and polycystic ovary syndrome. Causes of male infertility include abnormal sperm production or function, blockage of the epididymis, blockage of the ejaculatory ducts and hypospadias.

E1602.definition: An inflammatory process affecting a joint.

E160201.definition: A chronic systemic disease, primarily of the joints, marked by inflammatory changes in the synovial membranes and articular structures, widespread fibrinoid degeneration of the collagen fibers in mesenchymal tissues, and by atrophy and rarefaction of bony structures.

E1603.definition: A traumatic or pathological injury to the bone in which the continuity of the bone is broken.

E160301.definition: Traumatic or pathological injury to the hip in which the continuity of either the femoral head, femoral neck, intertrochanteric or subtrochanteric regions is broken.

E160302.definition: A traumatic break in one or more of the bones in a limb.

E160303.definition: Two or more simultaneous traumatic breaks in one or more bones.

E160304.definition: A traumatic or pathologic injury to the bones of the skull in which the continuity of the bones of the skull is broken.

E160305.definition: Traumatic or pathological injury to the spine in which the continuity of a vertebral bone is broken.

E1604.definition: A non-neoplastic or neoplastic disorder that affects the connective tissue.

E1605.definition: A sustained, sudden and involuntary contraction of a muscle or group of muscles.

E160501.definition: An involuntary muscular contraction involving a muscle of the abdomen or of a hollow organ within the abdomen.

E1606.definition: An injury to any of the fibrous bands of tissue that comprise an articulation (joint).

E1607.definition: Problem with mastication due to pain, discomfort or loss of mobility in the jaw.

E1609.definition: Inflammation and fibrous degeneration of a muscle.

E1610.definition: A traumatic injury to the head.

E1611.definition: Forceful extension of a joint beyond its normal limits.

E1612.definition: Insufficient structural and functional connection between living bone and the surface of a synthetic implant.

E161201.definition: Failure of the fixation of a prosthetic component in the absence of infection.

E1613.definition: Degenerative, pathological or traumatic changes in the cartilaginous tissue of the spine leading to unwanted compression or protrusion of the disc.

E1614.definition: An abnormal separation where two or more bones meet.

E161401.definition: Partial dislocation of the bones in a joint.

E1615.definition: Looseness or instability of a joint.

E1616.definition: A finding that the flexibility of a joint is below the expected range of normal for that individual.

E161601.definition: Immobility of the joint due to the formation of bone, cartilaginous or fibrous tissues around the joints.

E161602.definition: Permanent restriction of a joint, usually resulting from prolonged spasticity in a muscle area.

E161603.definition: An involuntary, persistent state of firm, tense muscles with marked resistance to passive movement.

E1617.definition: Faulty healing of bone, resulting in improper anatomical alignment.

E1618.definition: Also known as Metallosis. Includes trunnionosis, aseptic fibrosis or local necrosis secondary to metal corrosion and release of wear debris.

E1619.definition: Abnormally low level of muscle tone.

E1620.definition: Any injury to muscle or tendon tissue including strains.

E1621.definition: A reduction in the strength and/or mass of one or more muscles.

E1622.definition: Pain sensation originating from a muscle or group of muscles.

E1624.definition: Limited mobility of the neck, usually accompanied by pain.

E1625.definition: Broken bone that doesn't heal or is delayed in healing.

E1626.definition: The formation of bone or of a bony substance outside the normal skeleton. Includes ectopic or heterotopic ossification, myositis ossificans.

E1627.definition: Dissolution of bone; applied especially to the removal or loss of the calcium of bone.

E1628.definition: Infection of bone or bone marrow.

E1629.definition: Decreased calcification or density of bone tissue.

E1630.definition: An idiopathic inflammatory disorder affecting the muscles. It presents with symmetrical proximal muscle weakness and elevated skeletal muscle enzymes.

E1631.definition: Damage to the bones of the spine.

E1633.definition: Breakage of any portion of the tooth.

E1634.definition: Discrepancy between the lengths of the lower or upper extremities.

E1635.definition: The report describes a non-specific problem with the musculoskeletal system. Note: Please use "Appropriate Term / Code Not Available" if the report describes a specific problem but the relevant term does not exist.

E1636.definition: One or more teeth lost/dislodged from the mouth.

E1639.definition: Impingement relating to joints. Can be e.g. implant-on-bone, implant-on-soft tissue, or implant-on-implant impingement.

E1641.definition: Pain in the arms and/or legs.

E1701.definition: Superficial damage to the skin caused by rubbing or scraping.

E1702.definition: Rapid swelling of the deep layers of the skin due to transient vascular leakage of serous fluid.

E1703.definition: A collection of fluid underneath the top layer of skin.

E1704.definition: An injury or tissue damage caused by exposure to caustic chemicals, extreme heat, extreme cold or excessive radiation.

E170401.definition: A burn caused by exposure to chemical substances.

E170402.definition: Local tissue damage due to exposure to extreme cold.

E170403.definition: A burn caused by exposure to x-ray, radium, sunlight, ionizing radiation or any other type of radiant energy.

E170404.definition: A burn that affects the epidermis only, causing erythema without blistering.

E170405.definition: A burn that affects the epidermis and the dermis.

E170406.definition: A burn to the skin that extends into deeper layers and underlying tissues.

E1705.definition: A sensation of stinging or heat, not necessarily accompanied by redness or physical signs of irritation.

E170501.definition: A sensation of dermal stinging or heat, not necessarily accompanied by redness or physical signs of skin irritation.

E1706.definition: Spreading benign or malignant tissue during medical procedures.

E1707.definition: Improper repair of any body tissue due to factors affecting one or more of the phases of wound healing. Includes impaired healing of any body tissue.

E1708.definition: An irritating feeling that produces the desire to scratch.

E1709.definition: Yellow pigmentation of the skin, mucous membranes, and the eyes due to hyperbilirubinemia.

E1710.definition: A pathologic process that affects the skin and is confined to a specific area.

E1711.definition: A peeling off or loss of epidermis, as in sunburn, postscarlatinal peeling, or toxic epidermal necrolysis.

E1712.definition: A nonimmunologic, chemically induced type of photosensitivity.

E1713.definition: Erosion of patient's tissue pocket which houses a device.

E1714.definition: An eruption in the skin which effects its appearance and/or texture.

E1715.definition: Formation of new tissue formed in the healing of a wound.

E1716.definition: any abnormal change in skin coloration.

E171602.definition: Darkening of the skin due to excessive melanin deposition.

E171603.definition: Abnormal lightening of skin due to decreased melanin production or deposition.

E1718.definition: A gradual breakdown or very shallow ulceration of the skin which involves only the epidermis and heals without scarring.

E1719.definition: An inflammatory process affecting the skin, caused by bacteria, viruses, parasites, or fungi.

E1720.definition: An inflammatory process affecting the skin. Signs include red rash, itching, and blister formation. Representative examples are contact dermatitis, atopic dermatitis, and seborrheic dermatitis.

E172001.definition: An inflammatory process characterized by the accumulation of pus within a newly formed tissue cavity.

E172002.definition: Inflammation of the dermis and subcutaneous tissues caused by a bacterial infection.

E172003.definition: An inflammatory skin condition caused by direct contact between the skin and either an irritating substance or an allergen.

E172004.definition: A form of dermatitis characterized by red, itchy, scaly, or crusty patches that can be chronic or intermittent.

E172005.definition: A cutaneous inflammatory reaction occurring as a result of exposure to biologically effective levels of ionizing radiation.

E172006.definition: A transient, itchy skin eruption characterized by wheals with pale interiors and red margins.

E172007.definition: A smooth, slightly elevated area on the body surface, which is redder or paler than the surrounding skin.

E1721.definition: A break in skin tissue caused by friction or shearing.

E1722.definition: A small palpable abnormal mass in the subcutaneous tissues.

E1723.definition: A folding, ridge or creasing of the skin.

E1724.definition: Skin that has become dry in texture and flaky.

E1725.definition: Liquid or a pocket of air trapped under the skin, typically due to injection problems. Does not include inflammation.

E1726.definition: Softening of tissue by the action of a liquid. Occurs at the wound site/surrounding areas due to excessive moisture from exudate or products applied.

E1801.definition: A group of diseases in which abnormal cells divide without control, invade nearby tissues and may also spread to other parts of the body through the blood and lymph systems.

E180101.definition: A malignant neoplasm that develops or arises in breast tissue.

E180102.term: Breast Implant Associated Anaplastic Large Cell Lymphoma (BIA ALCL)
E180102.definition: A non-Hodgkin lymphoma which is associated with breast implants, and consists of large anaplastic cells. The WHO diagnostic criteria for BIA-ALCL includes positive expression of CD30 (CD30+) and negativity for anaplastic lymphoma kinase (ALK-).

E180104.definition: A malignant (clonal) proliferation of B- lymphocytes or T- lymphocytes which involves the lymph nodes, bone marrow and/or extranodal sites. This category includes Non-Hodgkin lymphomas and Hodgkin lymphomas.

E1802.definition: A sac-like closed membranous structure that may be empty or contain fluid or amorphous material.

E1803.definition: A small lump, swelling or collection of tissue.

E1804.definition: Abnormal mass of tissue that usually does not contain cysts or liquid areas. Solid tumours may be benign (not cancerous), or malignant (cancerous). Different types of solid tumours are named for the type of cells that form them. If tumours are associated with those under the term cancer, these terms should be used.

E1805.definition: A new and abnormal growth of tissue in a part of the body which is not indicative of malignant disorder. Can include benign tumors.

E1901.definition: An acute infectious disorder caused by gram positive or gram negative bacteria.

E190101.definition: An infection that is resistant to antibiotics and antimicrobials, for example, MRSA or VRE.

E190102.definition: An infection caused by pus-producing organisms.

E190103.definition: The condition resulting from the spread of bacterial products (toxins) by the bloodstream.

E1902.definition: An infection caused by a fungus.

E1903.definition: A disease acquired predominantly through sexual contact.

E1904.definition: Infection associated with no detectable signs or symptoms but caused by microorganisms capable of producing easily recognizable diseases.

E1905.definition: A group of rare degenerative brain disorders associated with prions for example Creutzfeldt-Jakob disease (CJD) or Bovine Spongiform Encephalopathy (BSE).

E1906.definition: The report describes a non-specific or unidentified infection. Note: Please use the appropriate term if the report describes a specific infection. i.e. Bacterial Infection E1901, Fungal Infection E1902, Viral Infection E1907, or a relevant Level 3 term where more detail is available.

E1907.definition: Any disease caused by a virus.

E190701.definition: A genus of the family herpesviridae, subfamily betaherpesvirinae, infecting the salivary glands, liver, spleen, lungs, eyes, and other organs, in which they produce characteristically enlarged cells with intranuclear inclusions.

E2002.definition: Injury of the soft tissues without breaking the skin that is characterized by blood leakage into the surrounding area.

E2003.definition: Contact with a chemical substance through touch, inhalation, or ingestion.

E2004.definition: Traumatic compression of the body or a part of the body.

E2005.definition: Appearance of bruises spontaneously or following minimal contact.

E2006.definition: An eating away or breakdown of any type of external or internal human tissue including but not limited to skin, teeth, mucosa, or somatic, which involves only the outer tissue layer. When tissue surrounds an implanted device, the tissue breakdown may result in migration and loss of the implant material and may result in further complications such as infection or abscess.

E2007.definition: A sudden movement downward, usually resulting in injury.

E2008.definition: An occurrence involving any object including device and/or fragments of device being left unintentionally in the body. This includes devices left in the body as part of risk mitigation or surgical bailout procedures since their presence or location is not as originally intended.

E200801.term: Device Embedded In Tissue or Plaque
E200801.definition: Device and/or fragments of device are embedded in patient's tissue and/or plaque.

E2009.definition: A cut or tear in any tissue.

E2010.definition: A penetrating stab wound from a needle (or other sharp object) that may result in exposure to blood or other body fluids.

E2011.definition: Patient becomes entangled or trapped in a device.

E2012.definition: Infection of a wound. This does not include post surgical wound infection.

E2013.definition: Forcible tearing or disruption of tissue.

E2014.definition: A process caused by injury or disease or aging and characterized by a partial/complete disruption of tissue. The disruption may be temporary or permanent and may be associated with either (1) impairment or (2) loss of function of the affected organ(s) or system(s).

E201401.definition: Damage to tissue due as a result of external pressure.

E2015.definition: The report describes a non-specific injury to the skin or subcutaneous tissue. Note: Please use "Appropriate Term / Code Not Available" if the report describes a specific injury but the relevant term does not exist.

E2101.definition: A fibrous band of tissue that connects normally separate body regions.

E2102.definition: A state of consciousness that permits the formation of explicit and implicit memories while under general anesthesia.

E2103.definition: A level of stimulation that is greater than the intended level.

E2104.definition: A shock caused by a brief, unintentional exposure to an electric current from a device.

E210401.definition: Unintended electric shock from patient leads. This includes an electric shock to a healthcare professional or a patient receiving a shock to an incorrect area of their body.

E2105.definition: Exposed to or contacted with blood or body fluids of another person.

E2106.definition: Pain that is associated with an external artificial replacement device.

E2108.definition: Failure of a surgically-induced connection between tubular structures in the body. Includes Anastomotic Leakage

E2109.definition: Pain localized to the site of the implanted device.

E2110.definition: Continuing discomfort due to a lack or failure of a medical approach to treat pain.

E2111.definition: An intense reaction (usually immunologic) developing at the site of injection

E2112.definition: Pain occurring during a surgical operation.

E2113.definition: A level of sedation that is greater than the intended level.

E2114.definition: A hole or opening made through a membrane or other tissue or material.

E211401.definition: A rupture in the organ(s) due to traumatic or pathologic processes.

E2115.definition: Infection of a surgical skin incision.

E2116.definition: The complex of symptoms characterizing the disease known as radiation injury, resulting from excessive exposure of the whole body (or large part) to ionizing radiation.

E2117.definition: Dislodgement, breakdown, or other malfunction of an artificial cardiac pacemaker, chemotherapy port, drip infusion valve, or similar implanted diagnostic or therapeutic device as a result of unconscious or habitual manipulation by the patient.

E2118.definition: The removal of a previously inserted tube from a hollow organ or passageway, often from the airway.

E2119.definition: The unintentional exposure to radiation of a person, or a part of a persons body. This might include exposure of a healthcare professional, or the exposure of the wrong part of the body of a patient who was intended to receive therapeutic or diagnostic radiation. This includes both ionizing and non ionizing radiation.

E2120.definition: A rare and potentially fatal perioperative complication of cemented bone surgery, characterised by hypotension, hypoxia, cardiac dysrhythmias, and in severe cases cardiac arrest.

E2121.definition: The observed patient condition is persistent blood flow/pressure in the aneurysm sac following an endovascular aneurysm repair (EVAR) procedure.  Where other patient signs and symptoms indicate the presence of an endoleak those signs and symptoms should be coded.

E2122.definition: Inflammation (swelling and redness) of the paranasal sinuses, associated or related to implantation procedures or devices.

E2123.definition: Infection local to an implanted or invasive medical device.

E2202.definition: A high level of the degree to which oxygen is bound to hemoglobin given as a percentage calculated by dividing the maximum oxygen capacity into the actual oxygen content and multiplying by 100. Oxygen saturation usually is measured using pulse oximetry.

E2203.definition: A low level of the degree to which oxygen is bound to hemoglobin given as a percentage calculated by dividing the maximum oxygen capacity into the actual oxygen content and multiplying by 100. Oxygen saturation usually is measured using pulse oximetry.

E2204.definition: A laboratory test result indicating an increase in the lactate dehydrogenase concentration of a biological sample.

E2205.definition: Condition that relates to the presence of viable bacteria in the bloodstream, whether associated with active disease or not.

E2206.definition: High blood or serum levels of ions which are attributed to one or more medical devices used, such as but not limited to Co, Cr, Ti, Ni, Mo.

E2301.definition: A Change or alteration of Body Temperature to a temperature outside the range of normal body temperature.

E230101.definition: Elevation of body temperature above normal due to the bodies own responses.

E230102.definition: An abnormally high body temperature. Not fever.

E2302.definition: Any persistent problem with walking, gait or maintaining posture (sitting, standing).

E2303.definition: The tightening of scar tissue that forms around the implant.

E2304.definition: Shivering or moderate tremors of the body often accompanied by a cold sensation.

E2305.definition: A bluish or purplish discoloration of the skin and mucous membranes resulting from a reduced amount of oxygenated hemoglobin in the blood.

E2308.definition: An alteration of appearance, shape, size or alignment.

E2309.definition: Accumulation of extraneous inorganic matter in tissues or cavities.

E230901.definition: Deposition of calcium salt in the tissues.

E2311.definition: A feeling of mental or physical uneasiness, pain, or distress.

E2312.definition: A state of generalized weakness with a pronounced inability to summon sufficient energy to accomplish daily activities.

E231201.definition: Extreme fatigue; the inability to respond to stimuli.

E2314.definition: Abnormal epithelial-lined communication between two anatomical structures.

E2315.definition: Flow or leakage of fluid other than blood, from an orifice, wound or tissue.

E231501.definition: A flow or draining of pus or exudate from an orifice or wound.

E2316.definition: An inflammatory reaction evoked by the presence of an exogenous material in the tissues.

E2317.definition: An inflammatory reaction usually caused by infectious organisms, foreign bodies, or cholesterol deposits. It is characterized by the presence of epithelioid histiocytes and chronic inflammation.

E2318.definition: Loss of hair usually from the scalp that may result in bald spots or spread to the entire scalp or epidermis.

E2319.definition: The protrusion of part of an organ or fibroadipose tissue through an opening or weakened area.

E2320.definition: Blood pressure that is abnormally high.

E2321.definition: Blood pressure that is abnormally low.

E2322.definition: The presence of an increased amount of blood in a part or organ; engorgement or bloodshot

E2323.definition: An abnormal increase in the number of cells in an organ or a tissue with consequent enlargement.

E2324.definition: Involuntary passage of feces and/or urine from the body.

E232401.definition: Inability to control voluntary passage of feces from the body.

E232402.definition: Inability to control voluntary passage of urine from the body.

E2325.definition: Permeation of foreign substances into tissues or cells.

E2326.definition: A localized physical condition in which part of the body becomes reddened, swollen, or hot and often painful.

E2327.definition: The pathologic death of cells or of a portion of tissue or organ resulting from irreversible damage.

E2328.definition: Blockage or closing of the normal flow of the contents of an anatomical passageway.

E2329.definition: A splitting open or rupture of an internal organ with the exposure or discharge of its content.

E2330.definition: An unpleasant sensory and emotional experience that is associated with actual or potential tissue damage or described in such terms.

E2331.definition: Unhealthy, pale or white appearance of the face.

E2332.definition: Lack or absence of balanced proportions between parts or organs of the body.

E2333.definition: A condition in which an organ or body tissue drops or bulges out of place.

E2334.definition: The drooping or downward displacement of a body part.

E2335.term: Reaction to Medicinal Component of Device
E2335.definition: Any local or systemic adverse reaction to the medicinal component of a combination product.

E2336.definition: A life-threatening condition that requires immediate medical intervention. It is characterized by reduced blood flow that may result in damage of multiple organs.

E233601.definition: Shock resulting from primary failure of the heart in its pumping function, as in myocardial infarction, severe cardiomyopathy, or mechanical obstruction or compression of the heart.

E233602.definition: A hypoglycemic reaction to overdosage of insulin, a skipped meal, or strenuous exercise in an insulin-dependent diabetic.

E233603.definition: Shock resulting from insufficient blood volume for the maintenance of adequate cardiac output, blood pressure and tissue perfusion.

E233604.definition: Shock resulting from neurogenic vasodilation, which can be produced by cerebral trauma or hemorrhage, spinal cord injury, deep general or spinal anesthesia, or toxic central nervous system depression.

E233605.definition: A state of acute circulatory failure resulting from organ injury or damage in response to infection that results in dangerously low blood pressure.

E2337.definition: Narrowing or stricture of a vessel, duct or canal.

E233701.definition: The reoccurrence of stenosis after it has been treated.

E2338.definition: Enlargement or expansion in size of a body part from injury or inflammation.

E233801.definition: accumulation of fluid in tissues perfused by the peripheral vascular system.

E233802.definition: An abnormal collection of fluid in hollow spaces or between tissues of the joints.

E2339.definition: An open sore on an external or internal surface of the body caused by a break in the skin or mucous membrane that fails to heal.

E2340.definition: A complication in which the wound splits or separates after being surgically closed.

E2341.definition: The presence of two distinct capsular layers around an implant with an intercapsular space

E2342.definition: Complete impairment of two or more organs or organ systems. Also known as multiple organ failure.

E24.term: Other Terms/Codes Related to Clinical Signs and Symptoms or Conditions

E2401.definition: It is not clear whether any health effects occurred, or health effect appears to have occurred but there is not yet enough information available to classify the clinical signs, symptoms and conditions.

E2402.term: Appropriate Clinical Signs, Symptoms and Conditions Term/Code Not Available
E2402.definition: The clinical signs, symptoms and conditions are not adequately described by any other term. Note: this code must not be used unless there is no other feasible code. The preferred term should be documented when submitting an adverse event report. This information will be used to determine if a new term should be added to the code table.

E2403.term: No Clinical Signs, Symptoms or Conditions
E2403.definition: No patient involvement or, no observable clinical symptoms or a change in symptoms is identified in the patient.
